subject: Hex OS suites: a 'detached Frame' flake survives the ephemeral-port fix
description:
Nancy saw it once in four runs and labelled it SUSPECTED, believing it was contention. I found and fixed a REAL contention bug (all 11 hexos suites bound fixed ports; two collided on 9311; reproduced two concurrent runs -> one 132/132, one EADDRINUSE) and after the fix ran all 11 simultaneously clean. But Chris, re-running the same concurrency check independently during the deploy gate, hit a 'detached Frame' crash again. So the port collision and the frame detachment are TWO DIFFERENT problems and only the first is fixed. The remaining one is most likely browser/memory contention when many puppeteer instances share this machine, not a race in the shell's watchdog. Do NOT close this by re-running until green: that is the exact behaviour phantom failures train. Next step is to instrument which page/frame is being torn down and whether it correlates with instance count or with the multi-generation lock test specifically (hex-shell-process.test.js around the pg3 open).
[2026-09-06 04:05] MEASURED 2026-09-05, trigger still NOT reproduced. Three repros run: (1) deferred r.respond() firing after page.close() does NOT crash puppeteer 24 -- hypothesis ELIMINATED, not assumed away. (2) When a page's target dies mid-wait, page.waitForFunction rejects with 'Waiting failed: 5000ms exceeded' -- a PLAIN TIMEOUT, indistinguishable from a genuine assertion failure. waitForText's catch (:218) then does a fallback read that assumes timeout; on a dead page that fallback ITSELF throws 'Protocol error (Runtime.callFunctionOn): Target closed' and ESCAPES the helper. The recovery path destroys the diagnosis. (3) Under a REAL renderer OOM (--max-old-space-size=64, allocate until death), page.on('error') FIRED with 'Page crashed!' while isClosed() stayed FALSE and browser.connected stayed TRUE. So page.on('error') is the ONLY signal that sees the contention failure mode; any design keyed on isClosed() or browser.connected would MISS it. Also measured: teardown took 107 SECONDS after an OOM, so a wedged browser can hang the gate rather than fail it. CALLERS: TWO, not one -- deploy.sh gate 3.7 (:430) AND post-verify.sh check 4f (:424). I claimed one and was wrong; grep -rn from repo root skips gitignored _tools/ (see reference_grep_skips_gitignored_tools.md) and the suite's own @catalog note header already said 'plus post-verify check 4f'. EXIT CODE 2 IS UNAVAILABLE: seven post-verify call sites (231,414,426,443,457,473,489) map rc 2 to 'skip, puppeteer unavailable' with NO divergence flag, and four sibling suites exit 2 for that. Redefining it would make a mid-run harness fault silently skip POST-DEPLOY verification against live production. Plan is now instrument-only, zero semantic change: register page.on('error') per page with a label, and log page forensics from unhandledRejection/uncaughtException handlers that exit 1 (node's own default for both, measured) so every consumer sees identical behaviour. Does NOT fix the flake; makes the next occurrence diagnosable.
[2026-09-06 04:26] CAPTURED THE REAL EVENT 2026-09-06 00:18:40, with forensics. PROVENANCE CAVEAT FIRST: this fired ~when I TaskStop'd a prior sweep, and killing the bash job takes Chromium down with it, so this specific capture is PROBABLY MY OWN KILL rather than a wild occurrence. It is still the first time an 'Attempted to use detached Frame' has been characterised here at all, and the signature is the finding. Forensics: pg1-main, crash=none, closed=false, url=http://127.0.0.1:PORT/hex/index.html, browser.connected=FALSE. Stack: CdpPage.evaluate -> run() (now line 341, 'await pg.evaluate' clearing #out) <- caller 'o = await run(\"search course\")' (now line 570). EVERY STANDING THEORY IS WRONG: task 345 guessed 'around the pg3 open' and the SITREP suspected the pg5 watchdog block -- it was pg1-main, an ordinary mid-suite assertion. crash=none means NO renderer crash, so the 'browser/memory contention crashes a renderer' theory is not what this was. closed=false means the page was not torn down. The one abnormal value is browser.connected=false: THE BROWSER PROCESS DIED, and every subsequent page.evaluate then throws detached Frame wherever the suite happens to be. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE TASK'S OWN ASK: 'which page/frame is torn down' has a deflationary answer -- the page identity is incidental, the diagnostic that matters is browser.connected. NEW LEADING HYPOTHESIS for the wild flake: the Chromium PROCESS dies (OOM-killer under concurrency), not a renderer crashing inside it. This box has 7940MB total / ~3983MB available and Chris saw the flake during an 11-suite concurrency check; 11 Chromiums against that headroom is exactly the pressure that invites a kernel kill. dmesg is not readable unprivileged here so the OOM hypothesis is UNTESTED. Next experiment: run the 16 hexos suites concurrently N times and check the fault logs for browser.connected=false.
[2026-09-06 04:57] PHASE 1 SHIPPED (committed, NOT deployed - no _app change, nothing student-facing). b97550e70 suite forensics + deploy.sh gate 3.7 reclassification; dff20aa80 post-verify check 4f, the same misattribution one file over that a reviewer found only AFTER the first fix landed. 345 STAYS OPEN: this does not fix the flake, it makes an occurrence diagnosable and stops it reading as a shell regression. Evidence behind it: 6 consecutive clean runs at 132/132 rc 0 on the pre-teardown-fix code, 3 more at 132/132 rc 0 on final code, baseline 132/132 rc 0 2m33s vs ~2m35s after; suite mtime pre-registered BEFORE each window and re-stat'd identical after, so 'not edited while measuring itself' is checkable rather than asserted. Fault path driven by INJECTION in both directions (before the tally -> 'NOTHING WAS VERIFIED'; during teardown after a clean tally -> 'the shell WAS verified'), and the output piped through both callers' real filters (tail -3; grep -E 'FAIL|passed' | tail -5) because a plain dump would have been truncated by the first and dropped ENTIRELY by the second. Adversarial reviewer PAUSED three times and PROCEEDed; Chris PASSED after running the suite himself and rebuilding the two-branch logic in his own probe. TWO MISSES OF MINE WORTH REMEMBERING: (1) I claimed gate 3.7 was the only caller when post-verify check 4f is a second one, because grep -rn from the repo root skips gitignored _tools/ and the suite's own @catalog header already said so; (2) I fixed the log body and deploy.sh but left post-verify's headline, the same 'fix the field beside the one you fixed' pattern, caught by the second reviewer. Also: the repo QC hook correctly blocked a half-applied edit that declared a variable with a comment describing behaviour not yet written, and my first teardown-branch test was INVALID (the scratchpad copy could not resolve _app so the suite died before the injection; the tell was no tally line in the output) - I nearly reported it as a pass.
[2026-09-06 05:00] CONCURRENCY PROBE: NEGATIVE RESULT, and it argues AGAINST my own leading hypothesis. Ran all 11 Chromium-launching hexos suites SIMULTANEOUSLY, 2 rounds, 22 suite runs total, 362 assertions per round (hex-shell-process 132, md100-cmdlet-help 58, doc-examples 38, tenant-crosstab 32, pwa 24, tenant-containment 19, safe-entry 18, whatsnew-tenant 13, first-timer 11, terminal-async-output 10, api-degradation-a11y 7). EVERY RUN rc=0. Zero 'detached Frame', zero 'Target closed', zero 'Page crashed', zero browser.connected=false, zero harness faults. THE FLAKE DID NOT REPRODUCE. MEMORY, sampled every 2s throughout: low-water 2405MB available in round 1 and 2581MB in round 2, on a 7940MB box. Eleven concurrent Chromiums never came close to exhausting it, so the OOM-killer theory -- my own leading hypothesis after the browser.connected=FALSE capture -- IS NOT SUPPORTED AT THIS CONCURRENCY LEVEL. Memory pressure is simply not what 11-way concurrency produces here. WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT ESTABLISH: it does NOT prove the flake is gone; 22 runs says little about an event nobody has reproduced on demand, and Chris saw it once during a comparable check. It DOES establish that 11-way concurrency ALONE, on an otherwise idle box, is not sufficient to trigger it -- so whatever the trigger is, it needs something this probe did not supply (other load on the machine, a different memory state, or something unrelated to contention entirely). Do NOT close this by running the probe until it goes red; that is the exact behaviour phantom failures train. One reporting artifact worth knowing for the next person: three suites (api-degradation-a11y, first-timer, terminal-async-output) print 'N passed, 0 failed' or 'N clean / 0 still broken' rather than 'N/M passed', so a probe grepping only the latter shows them BLANK. They had asserted correctly; the blank was the probe's regex, not a silent no-op. Verified by reading their output rather than trusting the empty column.
